title: REQ-01: Match clock with quarter management
body:
## Requirement

Keep time for the playing of the game.

## Source

Product Owner brief, requirement 1. Clock behaviour confirmed by PO: runs continuously within a quarter, hard stop at quarter end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Match configurable to 40, 50 or 60 total minutes
- [ ] Quarter count configurable (default 4), quarters must be equal length
- [ ] Invalid combinations (not evenly divisible) rejected with a clear message
- [ ] Clock runs continuously within a quarter; no routine pause
- [ ] Clock stops automatically at quarter end
- [ ] Manual pause available as an exception control, visually de-emphasised
- [ ] Elapsed time computed from wall-clock anchors, never from tick counting
- [ ] Time survives app backgrounding, screen lock and process death with zero loss
- [ ] Relaunch into an in-progress match offers a resume prompt showing computed elapsed time
- [ ] Quarter can be ended early by the coach; actual elapsed recorded, not nominal

## Notes

The wall-clock derivation is the critical detail — a timer-callback counter silently loses time when Android throttles background JS, which would corrupt the fairness ledger.

See `docs/specs/02-match-engine.md`.

title: REQ-02: Assign players to positions and track position time
body:
## Requirement

Assign players to positions and track their time in those positions.

## Source

Product Owner brief, requirement 2.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Customisable format; 7-a-side is the default
- [ ] Position set editable (labels, count, sort order)
- [ ] Exactly one position may be of kind `goalkeeper`
- [ ] Players assignable to positions via a pitch view
- [ ] Same player cannot occupy two positions; rejected with validation error
- [ ] Time accrued per position as well as per player, for reporting
- [ ] Per-position time is descriptive only — never used for fairness or anomaly detection
- [ ] Position change closes the current Appearance and opens a new one
- [ ] Position kind snapshotted on the Appearance so later format edits cannot rewrite history
- [ ] Vacant position (injury with no replacement) recorded explicitly, not silently backfilled

See `docs/specs/01-domain-model.md`.

title: REQ-03: Track total minutes played per player
body:
## Requirement

Track overall minutes played of every player playing.

## Source

Product Owner brief, requirement 3.

PO decisions: fairness is measured on total playing time, not per position. Goalkeeper time is tracked separately and excluded from the fairness measure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live minutes visible per player during a match
- [ ] Total outfield minutes (all positions combined) displayed — this is the fairness figure
- [ ] Goalkeeper minutes displayed as a separate figure, excluded from fairness
- [ ] Per-position breakdown available for reporting, not used as a measure
- [ ] Bench time recorded explicitly via BenchStint, not inferred by subtraction
- [ ] Invariant enforced: every available player is in exactly one of an open Appearance or open BenchStint at any elapsed time
- [ ] Quarter totals reconcile: sum of Appearance durations equals quarterMinutes x onFieldCount
- [ ] All totals derived by folding intervals; never stored as an authored running total

## Notes

Deriving rather than storing totals is what guarantees the displayed number and the audit trail can never disagree — essential for the dispute arbitration requirement.

See `docs/specs/01-domain-model.md`.

title: REQ-04: Substitution admin with sub-due alerting
body:
## Requirement

Provide a substitution admin that swaps a player for a subs bench player, allows swapping a player's position on field, and tracks planned sub/player time on the pitch, alerting when a sub is due.

## Source

Product Owner brief, requirement 4. Alerting design shaped by PO's note that the clock cannot be reliably stopped at stoppages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Swap an on-field player for a bench player in a single interaction
- [ ] Swap two on-field players' positions
- [ ] Substitution is instantaneous: outgoing interval closes and incoming opens at the same elapsed instant
- [ ] Plan sub timings in advance per quarter
- [ ] Alarm raised when a planned sub falls due
- [ ] Alarm is a standing flag that persists until actioned or quarter end, not a dismissable instant notification
- [ ] Alarm wording frames action at the next break in play
- [ ] Late-actioned subs record true time; planned-vs-actual variance retained and surfaced
- [ ] Unactioned alarm escalates visual prominence after a configurable threshold (default 3 min)
- [ ] Subs unactioned at quarter end carry into the next quarter's planned team sheet
- [ ] Optional haptic and sound alongside visual alert

## Notes

Background notifications are out of MVP scope — the app is expected to be open and foregrounded during a match.

See `docs/specs/02-match-engine.md`.

title: REQ-05: Quarter close with next team sheet and last-minute adjustment
body:
## Requirement

Closing of a quarter should stop the clock and bring up the next planned team sheet, but allow for last-minute adjustments.

## Source

Product Owner brief, requirement 5.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Quarter end stops the clock automatically
- [ ] All open Appearances and BenchStints close at the quarter boundary
- [ ] Next quarter's planned team sheet presented immediately
- [ ] Team sheet fully editable before the coach confirms
- [ ] Carried-over unactioned subs pre-applied to the suggested sheet
- [ ] Projected end-of-match fairness balances shown before confirming
- [ ] Quarter cannot start until exactly onFieldCount distinct positions are filled
- [ ] Unfilled positions named explicitly in the blocking message
- [ ] Coach override of a suggested sheet recorded with optional reason

See `docs/specs/02-match-engine.md`.

title: REQ-06: Match event capture (goal, save, tackle, foul)
body:
## Requirement

Capture key events from coaches in a match: goal, save, tackle, foul, with timestamps.

## Source

Product Owner brief, requirement 6 — explicitly a later iteration, but to be borne in mind during MVP design.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] MatchEvent entity with type, elapsedMs, playerId, positionId
- [ ] Event types: goal, save, tackle, foul (extensible)
- [ ] One-tap capture during live play without disrupting the clock
- [ ] Events attributable to the position the player held at that instant
- [ ] Events reviewable and correctable post-match

## MVP design constraint

The MVP clock is modelled as accumulated `elapsedMs` specifically so this is a pure addition requiring no migration of existing entities. Do not regress that property.

See `docs/specs/01-domain-model.md`.

title: REQ-07: Season fairness ledger with equal time allocation
body:
## Requirement

Each player gets an equal allocation of **total playing time** over a multi-match period or season, allowing anomalies to be fixed over time.

## Source

Product Owner, in response to clarifying questions.

PO correction (2026-09-17): *"Fairness wasn't supposed to be per position, just total playing time. We are likely to lock players into certain positions or a couple of positions so their distribution will be higher into those affinities."*

PO decision: goalkeeper time is excluded from the fairness measure entirely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Season entity grouping matches for a squad
- [ ] Per-player season totals derived by folding all Appearances, never authored
- [ ] Fairness balance computed as actual minus expected **total outfield** time
- [ ] Outfield minutes summed across all positions; position plays no part in the calculation
- [ ] **No fairness arithmetic and no anomaly flags on per-position distribution**
- [ ] Goalkeeper minutes excluded from the fairness measure
- [ ] A player keeping for part of a match accrues expected time scaled to their outfield-eligible portion
- [ ] Expected time accrues only for matches where the player was available
- [ ] Balances carry across matches within a season, reset between seasons
- [ ] Mid-season joiners start at zero and accrue expected time from their first available match
- [ ] Team-sheet builder sorts available squad most-owed first
- [ ] Suggested sub schedule drives balances toward zero by adjusting **duration**, never by moving a player out of their preferred position
- [ ] Projected balances shown before the coach confirms a plan

## Notes

Position affinity is deliberate coach policy. Measuring fairness per position would generate false anomalies against the coach's own selection decisions — this is the defining constraint of the feature.

See `docs/specs/03-fairness-ledger.md`.

title: REQ-08: Dispute arbitration record and audit trail
body:
## Requirement

Data recorded and observed for fairness and dispute arbitration.

## Source

Product Owner, in response to clarifying question on fair play time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-player record showing season totals (outfield = the fairness figure, GK separate), running balance match by match, and every individual Appearance with match, quarter, position, start, end and duration
- [ ] Appearances correctable after the fact
- [ ] Correction requires a mandatory note
- [ ] Original values retained in a correction log; corrections never destructive
- [ ] Ledger displays corrected figures but flags that corrections exist
- [ ] Coach overrides of suggested plans recorded with reasons
- [ ] Anomaly flags: persistent deficit, persistent surplus, correction cluster, short-handed match
- [ ] **No** position-distribution or never-keeper flags — these would fight deliberate position affinities
- [ ] Flags advisory only; nothing auto-corrected

## Open question for PO

Is CSV / printable export needed for MVP, or is on-screen review sufficient initially?

See `docs/specs/03-fairness-ledger.md`.

title: REQ-09: Squad and player management (GDPR-minimal)
body:
## Requirement

Build a team of players, first names only for GDPR reasons. Squads of around 11 players with 7-a-side as the current setup.

## Source

Product Owner brief.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create and edit squads
- [ ] Add players with first name only
- [ ] No fields for surname, DOB, contact details or photographs anywhere in the model or UI
- [ ] Optional 2-character display suffix to disambiguate shared first names
- [ ] Optional squad number
- [ ] Players deactivatable without deletion, retaining ledger history
- [ ] Per-match availability: available, absent, injured, unavailable
- [ ] Squad size not hard-capped; 11 is typical, not enforced
- [ ] Position affinities recordable per player (primary / secondary)
- [ ] Players with no affinity treated as eligible for any outfield position
- [ ] Affinities constrain suggestions only; manual assignment always permitted

## Notes

The 2-character cap on the disambiguation suffix is deliberate — it prevents the field becoming a surname field by convention.

See `docs/specs/01-domain-model.md`.

title: REQ-10: Customisable match format and positions
body:
## Requirement

Player positions relate to a customisable setup, currently 7-a-side.

## Source

Product Owner brief.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Format entity with name, on-field count and ordered position list
- [ ] 7-a-side seeded as the default format
- [ ] Position labels, kinds and ordering editable
- [ ] Position list length must equal on-field count
- [ ] At most one goalkeeper position per format
- [ ] Format snapshotted onto a match at creation so later edits do not rewrite history
- [ ] Pitch view lays out positions by sort order

See `docs/specs/01-domain-model.md`.

title: TECH-01: Expo + TypeScript project scaffold
body:
## Task

Scaffold the React Native + Expo application.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expo project with TypeScript in strict mode
- [ ] Navigation configured
- [ ] State management chosen and wired
- [ ] Local persistence layer with a migration path
- [ ] ESLint and Prettier configured
- [ ] Test runner configured with a passing example test
- [ ] `.gitignore` blocking common data-file patterns, so squad data cannot be committed accidentally
- [ ] Runs on an Android device via Expo Go
- [ ] README with setup and run instructions

## Notes

iOS support is a stated future aspiration — avoid Android-only APIs in shared code without an abstraction.

title: TECH-02: Match engine core with full test suite
body:
## Task

Implement the match engine as pure TypeScript, independent of React, with comprehensive tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clock, quarters, Appearances, BenchStints and minutes accumulation implemented as pure functions over state
- [ ] No React or platform dependencies in the engine module
- [ ] Wall-clock derivation; no tick counting
- [ ] Invariant tests: player continuity, quarter total reconciliation, no double-counting across substitutions
- [ ] Worked fairness example from the spec encoded as an executable test
- [ ] Test asserting fairness is position-independent: two players with identical total minutes in entirely different positions have identical balances
- [ ] Test asserting GK minutes do not alter a player's fairness balance
- [ ] Edge case tests: injury with no replacement, short-handed match, abandoned match, early quarter end, duplicate position assignment, correction applied after the fact
- [ ] Property-based tests over random substitution sequences asserting invariants hold

## Notes

Keeping the engine pure is what makes the iOS port and the later events feature cheap, and makes the fairness maths verifiable without a device.
